title.text: How to read a written form

phrase.text: A written form is the mould of a construct: it says which words are fixed, which slots you fill in and which parts you may leave out.

runs.text: A written form is the mould of a construct: it says which words are fixed, which slots you fill in and which parts you may leave out.
Every language construct is first shown with its form. Coloured words are written exactly as shown. Slots
are replaced by code. Whatever goes between ⟦ and ⟧ is optional: you may write it or not.

blocks.description: At the top, the If form: the word If and the word Then are fixed, and between them there is a dashed slot called condition. An arrow goes down from the slot to the filled line If n > 0 Then. At the bottom, Else appears between double brackets: it is an optional part that can be left out.

caption.text: A form has fixed words and slots. Filling the slots gives a line of code; whatever goes between ⟦ and ⟧ you may leave out.
